selection_statements.text: The poster reports four cases transitioned to neonatal life, but does not report the total number entering FLI support or an attempted-transition denominator.
selection_statements.source_locator: Poster PDF, Results and conclusion; four-row outcome table

limitations: This is a candidate, typed transcription of a public conference poster, not a peer-reviewed full-cohort report or raw-data release; the poster table was visually inspected and all extracted values remain source-reported.

Only four poster-labeled transition cases are represented. The total FLI-start denominator and transition-eligible denominator are not reported, so these cases do not define a transition or survival rate.

The poster table visually prints support durations of 9, 24, 8 and 7 days. The four values have mean 12.0 days and sample SD 8.04 days, unlike the reported 9.6 ± 3.1-day cohort summary. Animal 2 gestational ages imply 14 days; Animal 4 gestational ages differ by 10 days while its FLI duration is 7 days. The poster does not reconcile the clock differences. Replacing 24 with 14 would yield a mean of 9.5 and sample SD 3.11, but remains an unverified hypothesis, not a correction.

The poster says satisfactory respiratory parameters were present in all four animals, while the case table records no successful extubation for Animals 1 and 2. These may describe distinct endpoints because assessment conditions and support mode are unspecified; preserve both statements and do not equate satisfactory monitored parameters with extubation.

The maze comparison is reported for one case at 3 months, with no named instrument details, scoring, blinded assessment, or broader developmental domains. It is not evidence of comprehensive normal development.

The source labels Animal 1-4 are poster-local labels only and are not linked to the 2025 OC14.07 abstract, other poster cohorts, the named Gaia case, or company follow-up claims. The close 9.6 ± 3.1-day poster support summary and 9.5 ± 3.3-day 2025 survival summary make partial overlap or follow-up plausible, but endpoint frames differ and no animal IDs/date crosswalk is reported; do not assume an independent replication or pool denominators.

Extubation, survival, disposition, support duration, and maze rows preserve separate source statements. Missing extubation times for Animals 1 and 2 remain unset; multiple endpoints are not collapsed into a single timepoint.

The poster table lists weights of 2.8, 2.0, 2.2 and 2.7 kg for Animals 1-4. The measurement timepoint is not stated; the candidate preserves the values with time unset and does not call them birth weight or transition weight.
